key_claims: Bin Ladin is the ultimate decisionmaker in al-Qa'ida and is directly involved in planning terrorist operations.
Muhammad 'Atif (Abu Hafs the Egyptian) is Bin Ladin's deputy and manages day-to-day operations.
Al-Qa'ida is structured on paper like a mini-state, with a Leadership Council, an Executive Council and committees such as the Military Committee.
Al-Qa'ida's network in about 60 countries and its allied groups let it run more than one major operation at once.
Al-Qa'ida builds ties through Afghan training programs, aid to insurgent movements and exploitation of contacts in some Islamic NGOs.
Dispersed key personnel such as Khalid Fawwaz in London help the network regroup if Bin Ladin has to move his headquarters.
